# Rust stable 1.99.0 core::net acceptance

The whole stable `core::net` API of Rust 1.99.0 was inventoried against its documented contract, RFC 4291, 5952, 4007 and 6874, and the supplied IANA registry snapshots. The subject is the installed standard library, rustc b940084d7 (2026-09-28); mutation controls use a separate source copy with [recorded shims](acceptance/PORTING.md). The [coverage receipt](acceptance/evidence/gen/coverage.json) records 600 API items, 51 RFC/documentation clauses and six additional behaviours; 499 rows remain explicit gaps.

**19 of 100 mutants survived rust-lang's own tests: 12 behavioural cases (7 distinct behaviours; the six whitespace cases are one rule) and 7 optional representation snapshots.**

[MISSING-TESTS.md](acceptance/MISSING-TESTS.md) separates the behavioural gaps from the optional representation regression tests. The [main coretests patch](acceptance/coretests-net.patch) contains the 12 behavioural tests, beside related existing tests after the imports. The [optional patch](acceptance/coretests-net-optional.patch) contains seven representation snapshots at each file's end. The FromStr impls are heavily tested in coretests `parser.rs:25–110` and `ip_addr.rs:9–120`; only leading-whitespace rejection is missing for those six witnesses. The other cases concern maximum-scope parsing, SocketAddr::set_ip metadata retention, IPv6 multicast flag bits, SocketAddr enum Display delegation, single-group compression input and hexadecimal leading-zero input.

Error text and the five Debug snapshots have no exact-output compatibility obligation. `core/src/fmt/mod.rs` says exactly: “Additionally, `Debug` implementations of types provided by the standard library (`std`, `core`, `alloc`, etc.) are not stable, and may also change with future Rust versions.” M095 separately observes an unresolved translated-prefix Display policy. [Patch receipts](acceptance/evidence/gen/patch-tests.txt) show all 19 additions passing on real std; [SCHEMATA.md](acceptance/SCHEMATA.md) records builds, wall times and per-test outcome agreement with historical run 3. M095's mutation semantics were corrected after that run.

No MUST or grammar deviation was reproduced in the finite corpus. [FINDINGS.md](acceptance/FINDINGS.md) supplies inputs, clauses and known-item checks.

| Class | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| DOCUMENTED | IPv6 link-local classification uses /10 and excludes loopback; socket input scopes use raw decimal syntax. Flowinfo omission from Display is an observed policy consistent with the documented input grammar. |
| KNOWN | `to_ipv4` extracts `::1` and `::`, consistent with its documented rule; #42174 matches the loopback observation. |
| AMBIGUOUS | RFC 5952 §5 mixed-notation applicability remains unresolved for compatible and RFC 2765 translated addresses. Compatible hexadecimal Display is a deliberate, tested upstream choice. |

The 143 weighted claims in [acceptance.toml](acceptance/acceptance.toml) apply only to their bounded assertions. Each control fails at runtime while the original copy and real std pass; upstream detection determines the missing-case list independently of weight. Optional representation assertions measure current output, not standards compliance or future stability.

## Confirmed in rust-lang's own tree

The final [review-session summary](acceptance/evidence/intree/replay/summary.json) records **66 baseline core net tests passed; 19 applied; each detected only by the added tests; all 47 existing net coretests and 105 doc tests stay green; 0 skipped**. The [baseline log](acceptance/evidence/intree/replay/baseline-coretests.txt) runs the combined 19 additions before the patch split (47 existing + 12 behavioural + 7 optional = 66). The split patches were checked with `git apply --check`; no native tests were rerun for the split. Each mutant fails its own added test, including the revised payload-preserving [M095](acceptance/evidence/intree/replay/M095-coretests.txt). [M092](acceptance/evidence/intree/replay/M092-coretests.txt) also fails the added Debug test; the other 18 fail only their own added test. No existing core net test fails. All native core::net doc groups stay green: **105 passing examples per mutant**. This includes examples excluded from the standalone 80-test doc port. [Native evidence](acceptance/evidence/intree/README.md) links every per-mutant receipt. The earlier `intree/logs/b` receipts copied into the parent evidence directory are historical; they predate the final patch and revised M095.

## Re-run

The [clean-copy replay](acceptance/evidence/gen/publication-replay.txt) reused a local validator checkout and installed toolchains. It did not clone over the network. The clone and pinned checkout commands below are the documented path for a new environment.

Prerequisites: git, rustup with toolchain **1.99.0**, **Python 3.14** available as `python3`, and `patch`. The tested host is **aarch64-apple-darwin**. Install the toolchain with `rustup toolchain install 1.99.0 --component rust-src`; install git, Python 3.14 and patch using the host's package manager. Obtain the validator from [ivmat/acceptance-format](https://github.com/ivmat/acceptance-format) and pin it:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ivmat/acceptance-format ../acceptance-format
git -C ../acceptance-format checkout e471a3c689cd1fec9d751a09972d1d785fb56765
export ACCEPTANCE_FORMAT=../acceptance-format
sh acceptance/run_all.sh
```

The runner verifies the validator pin, uses offline Cargo with a local Cargo home and `RUSTFLAGS="--cap-lints warn"`, and creates ignored targets and caches. It compiles 64 runtime mutants together and gives 36 const-dependent mutants separate builds; `NET_MUTANT=0` selects the original code. Repeat a single mutant with `cd acceptance && python3 runner.py --mutant M079`; repeat its original assertion with `python3 runner.py --case M079`. Conformance, strict core (including strict-weight) and strict verification validators must pass. They check record shape and hashes; source/toolchain checks supplement their subject-digest warning.

For native replay, prepare Rust's bootstrap dependencies and submodules before an offline run. A new checkout may require downloads during that preparation; no native build is part of run_all.sh. From this package's root:

```sh
git clone --branch 1.99.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/rust-lang/rust rust-tree
git -C rust-tree submodule update --init --recursive
python3 - <<'BOOTSTRAP'
from pathlib import Path
import json, subprocess
rustc = subprocess.check_output(['rustup', 'which', '--toolchain', '1.99.0', 'rustc'], text=True).strip()
cargo = subprocess.check_output(['rustup', 'which', '--toolchain', '1.99.0', 'cargo'], text=True).strip()
config = 'profile = "library"\nchange-id = "ignore"\n\n[build]\nrustc = '+json.dumps(rustc)+'\ncargo = '+json.dumps(cargo)+'\nlocal-rebuild = true\n\n[rust]\ndownload-rustc = false\n'
Path('rust-tree/bootstrap.toml').write_text(config)
BOOTSTRAP
export CARGO_HOME="$PWD/.cargo-home"
export RUSTFLAGS="--cap-lints warn"
git -C rust-tree apply ../acceptance/coretests-net.patch ../acceptance/coretests-net-optional.patch
(cd rust-tree && ./x test library/coretests --stage 1 -- net::)
(cd rust-tree && ./x test library/core --doc --stage 1 -- net)
git -C rust-tree apply -R ../acceptance/coretests-net.patch ../acceptance/coretests-net-optional.patch
sh acceptance/intree/run-intree.sh rust-tree
```

This is the review session's bootstrap configuration, with tool paths resolved locally: installed 1.99.0 stage 0 and `local-rebuild = true`. The portable runner verifies tag 1.99.0 and clean relevant files, applies each mutant by one unique exact text replacement, records all test-result groups, and restores original bytes. The review edit to `acceptance/intree/replay.py` inherits `CARGO_HOME`; `INTREE_CARGO_HOME` can select a different Cargo home already populated with Rust bootstrap dependencies. Both native test commands run offline. `--check-only` checks applicability without running `x` or changing files.

Patch regeneration additionally requires `rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-06-01 --component rustfmt`. Run `cd acceptance && python3 upstream_patch.py`. It uses Rust's bundled settings (a matching copy is in acceptance/intree/rustfmt.toml), records the rustfmt version and check, and checks each patch and both together with `git apply --check` when intree/rust is available. Files are formatted through stdin to avoid rustfmt's ignore-path panic when the config and files have different roots. No native tests are executed by that generator.

These are finite checks: [counts.json](acceptance/evidence/gen/counts.json) records 195,240 strings across six FromStr types (1,171,440 calls), 95,723 constructed addresses and 199 boundary obligations for 51 registry blocks, with seed 42915952. All 138 ported upstream tests and 100 proposed assertions pass on the original copy. Of 109 doc blocks, 80 run, 24 feature-gated examples are unported, four non-Rust blocks and one should_panic example are excluded; see [DOC-TESTS.md](acceptance/DOC-TESTS.md). Whole-tree search (review, 2026-10-09): the 1.99.0 coretests and benches, library/std net unit tests and TCP/UDP tests, core doc tests outside net, tests/ui, Miri, Clippy and rustfmt tests were searched by content. No covering assertion for any of the 19 named witnesses was found. Std net unit tests and Miri were checked by reading; they were not run under the mutants. No equivalent survivor was found. One small mutation per behaviour does not establish mutation adequacy; some assertions cover one enum branch or boundary. Stable const trait use, allocation failure, other targets and compiler internals are unchecked. Unstable methods remain only for the upstream port. Recommendation-level formatting choices remain unresolved.
